minutes.headline: Committee approved two budget transfers and a collaborative change, and agreed to hold a calendar workshop.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a memorial design update, approved line-item transfers for fuel oil, paper and security cameras, and advanced several policies. It gave final approval to the K-8 ELA curriculum and initial approval for a Nashville music trip. A long calendar debate ended with agreement to hold an interest-based workshop. Two executive sessions on collective bargaining were held.

what_happened.line: The School Committee gave final approval to the K-8 English language arts curriculum on its third reading.
After a long calendar debate, the committee settled on an interest-based workshop instead of revisiting the 2017-18 calendar.
The committee approved line-item transfers for fuel oil after a power outage, for paper supplies, and for security cameras at two schools.
The committee voted to approve North Middlesex joining the collaborative.
The committee gave initial approval to a Nashville music trip, with per-student cost described as tentative pending pricing.

why_it_matters: The transfers move money inside the school budget for fuel, supplies and building security, and the Nashville trip's per-student cost could fall on families if it stays high.
The ELA curriculum is now approved for every K-8 classroom, and the calendar workshop will shape future school-year dates for families.
watch_next: The interest-based school calendar workshop the committee agreed to hold.
Second reading of the athletic advisory council, school lunch and facilities use policies, and final pricing and approval for the Nashville trip.
